title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security on Severely Cracking Down on Illegal Publishing Crimes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court  Supreme People's Procuratorate  Ministry of Public Security

Notice on Severely Cracking Down on Criminal Activities of Illegal Publishing

Fa (Yan) Fa [1991] No. 5

High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and Public Security Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government:

With the deepening of the anti-pornography campaign, criminals who produce, sell, distribute, and smuggle pornographic materials have been cracked down upon to a certain extent. However, criminal activities of illegal publishing remain relatively serious. The prominent manifestations are: publications that have been explicitly banned for promoting obscenity, murder and violence, feudal superstition, and reactionary content have been reissued in a disguised form; some publishing units that have already been abolished are still engaging in illegal and criminal activities; individual publishing and distribution units continue to violate publishing management regulations, selling book and periodical numbers, and producing, soliciting subscriptions for, and distributing harmful books and periodicals in large quantities; some printing factories, blinded by profit, illegally accept orders to print illegal publications.

In order to severely punish criminal activities of illegal publishing according to law, on November 27, 1987, the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate issued the "Notice on Severely Punishing Criminal Activities of Illegal Publishing According to Law" (see page 17 of Issue 4, 1987 of this Gazette). Article 1 of that notice clearly stipulates: "Those who, for the purpose of seeking exorbitant profits, engage in the publishing, printing, distribution, or sale of illegal publications, where the illegal business turnover or illegal profits are relatively large and the circumstances are serious, shall be punished as the crime of speculation according to Article 117 of the Criminal Law; where the amounts are huge, Article 118 of the Criminal Law shall apply; where the circumstances are especially serious, the provisions of Item (1) of Article 1 of the 'Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy' shall apply." However, since the promulgation of this important judicial interpretation, some localities have not yet earnestly implemented it. In many cases that have already constituted crimes, they have not been transferred to the judicial organs for criminal responsibility, and the situation of substituting fines for criminal punishment remains serious. As a result, some criminals have not been subject to due punishment and continue to engage in criminal activities of illegal publishing. If this problem is not resolved, it will not only be detrimental to the deepening of the anti-pornography campaign, but will also jeopardize the achievements of the previous stage of the campaign, and may even cause the filthy tide of production and sale of pornographic materials to resurge.

It is hereby reiterated again: People's courts, people's procuratorates, and public security organs at all levels must strictly implement the provisions of Article 1 of the "Notice on Severely Punishing Criminal Activities of Illegal Publishing According to Law" of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate. With regard to the monetary standards for constituting the crime of speculation in illegal publishing activities other than the production, reproduction, and publishing of pornographic articles, before a new judicial interpretation is issued, the "Answers to Several Questions on the Specific Application of Law in Currently Handling Economic Crime Cases (for Trial Implementation)" of July 8, 1985, and the "Provisions on Currently Handling Cases of the Crime of Speculation Involving Enterprises, Institutions, State Organs, and Organizations" of March 15, 1989, both issued by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, shall still be followed. For cases of criminal illegal publishing, it must never be allowed that only administrative departments impose fines to settle the matter. Public security organs shall promptly file cases, conduct investigations, and transfer them to the people's procuratorates for review and prosecution; people's procuratorates and people's courts shall promptly accept them; people's courts shall, in accordance with the above-mentioned notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and in accordance with the Criminal Law and the relevant decisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, impose punishment. For units engaged in criminal activities of illegal publishing, criminal liability shall be pursued against the directly responsible supervisors and other persons directly responsible. Firmly correct and prevent the phenomena of "cases not being investigated, filed cases not being concluded, fines substituting for criminal punishment, and serious crimes being lightly sentenced." Efforts must be made to promptly handle a number of major and important cases, and through radio, television, newspapers, and other news media, expand publicity to suppress the arrogance of criminals and further deepen the anti-pornography campaign.

The above notice is expected to be seriously implemented. If any problems arise during implementation, please report them promptly.

January 30, 1991
